title: Finite-sum bilevel optimization with selectable original component gradients
summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

model.instance: (f,g,x0,y0) and declared oracle law; dimensions are arbitrary finite and minimax is over them

assumptions.description: Assume $f=(1/n_f)\sum_i f_i$. Each upper component's full gradient is jointly 1-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$. Only the average satisfies $\|\nabla_y f\|\le1$; individual $f_i$ partial gradients need not be bounded.

Assume $g=(1/n_g)\sum_j g_j$. Each lower-level component $g_j$ is twice continuously differentiable. Its full gradient and Hessian are jointly 1-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$, and it is mu-strongly convex in y for fixed x.
The reduced upper-level objective Phi is bounded below. The given x0 satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le1$, with a public fixed bound.
For each $i\in[n_f]$, the function $\nabla f_i$ is jointly 1-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$. Component Hessian Lipschitzness and bounded component-gradient variance are not assumed.
For every $j\in[n_g]$, $\nabla g_j$ and $\nabla^2g_j$ are jointly 1-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$, and $g_j(x,\cdot)$ is mu-strongly convex. Strong convexity of the average g alone is insufficient.

Given $\|y_0-y^*(x_0)\|\le R_{init}=1$, the algorithm sets $z_{init}=y_0,v_{init}=0$. The full scan used to compute the source initialization residual remains charged. This uniform certificate controls the initialization logarithm in the fixed-budget class.

resource.precision_model: Exact real arithmetic is assumed; the stochastic oracle has the stated noise. Bit complexity, memory, and arithmetic cost are not tracked.

bracket.ratio_or_gap:

notes: The affine lower-level solution $y^*(x)=(\kappa-1)x$ embeds a finite-sum bounded-gradient chain into bilevel stationarity, with amplification $\kappa-1$. Linear terms in upper- and lower-level component counts come from different hard families. The information lemma of Peng et al. has not been independently reproved. The source $\sqrt n$ is the upper-level component count and cannot be replaced by $\sqrt{n_f+n_g}$ for arbitrary splits.
